metadata.title: Common Shade - Map of heat risk finance
metadata.disclaimer: Listing is not endorsement and is not financial, insurance or investment advice.
metadata.scope: Targeted global landscape and category map; not exhaustive systematic review.
metadata.schema_note: User's seven top-level arrays retained. R1 instruments populated; selected schemes and triggers support examples. Other module arrays intentionally empty. Metadata, narrative, source register and exclusions are additive extensions.
metadata.unknown_convention: Not verified is not zero, no, never triggered or proof of exclusion. Empty payout arrays mean no quantified payout record admitted; consult payment_state.
metadata.evidence_note: Evidence labels describe kind, not scheme quality. Source publication by an independent institution is not automatically an independent impact evaluation.
metadata.money_convention: Amounts are separated by kind and transaction stage. USD amounts use FX 1; AXA uses explicitly declared fixed reporting conversion HKD 7.80/USD, not a historical transaction rate. Unknown original currency or FX means amount withheld.
metadata.mapping_note: Only supplied loop and lever IDs used. Mappings are analytical possibilities, not measured causal effects.
metadata.classification_note: One primary level and layer per instrument is a schema constraint. Premium support is a financing adjunct, outcomes payments are not necessarily risk finance, and social protection is a delivery/benefit system as well as a risk layer.

instruments.name: Parametric heat insurance - people
instruments.plain_definition: An insurer pays an agreed benefit when a specified heat index crosses the policy threshold, without assessing each person's actual income loss.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Cash can reduce pressure to work through dangerous heat; health and debt effects must be evaluated.
instruments.risk_holder: Insurer and reinsurer for contracted benefit; household retains uncovered losses.
instruments.who_pays: Member, employer or sponsor; identify separately by policy year.
instruments.who_receives: Insured person or a named beneficiary through the contracted channel.
instruments.speed: Index calculation avoids individual loss adjustment; days-to-cash is not verified for the example.
instruments.typical_cost: Risk premium plus distribution, data and servicing costs; no defensible universal price range.
instruments.strengths: Can insure income disruption without damaged property.
instruments.limits: Thresholds, caps and bank access can leave serious needs unfunded.
instruments.basis_risk: Location, metric and threshold may miss individual harm; payout can also exceed personal loss.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: SEWA establishes access for informal women members, not universal eligibility for poor households.

instruments.name: Parametric heat insurance - employers and organisations
instruments.plain_definition: A business or intermediary buys heat-triggered cover for its own costs or a specified group.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Pre-agreed benefits can support workers or operating liquidity; pass-through obligations matter.
instruments.who_receives: Organisation or covered workers; these are different arrangements.
instruments.speed: Potentially fast after index confirmation; published launch is not proof of payment speed.
instruments.typical_cost: Premium depends on trigger, season, benefit and population; AXA's launch price is recorded separately.
instruments.strengths: Aggregates buyers and may simplify enrolment.
instruments.limits: Employer receipt alone does not prove worker benefit; limited benefit can be mistaken for full wage replacement.
instruments.basis_risk: Regional weather data may miss worksite exposure.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Employer distribution can reach enrolled workers; informal, subcontracted and migrant access is not established.

instruments.name: Parametric heat insurance - sovereign design
instruments.plain_definition: A government transfers a defined heat-related fiscal risk using an agreed index.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: A contingent receipt could protect emergency budgets if release and spending rules are agreed.
instruments.risk_holder: Insurer/reinsurer for the policy limit; state retains residual risk.
instruments.who_receives: Treasury or designated public agency, then services or households.
instruments.speed: Design-dependent; no verified sovereign heat payout benchmark in this review.
instruments.typical_cost: Expected payout, capital charge, data/model, brokerage and administration; no verified heat quote.
instruments.strengths: Could fund health or income response without asset destruction.
instruments.limits: No issued sovereign heat policy was verified here; do not present the category as an operating scheme.
instruments.basis_risk: Fiscal spending and population harm may not track one temperature index.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Requires targeting and delivery systems beyond sovereign receipt.

instruments.name: Heat-related business interruption indemnity
instruments.plain_definition: Pays eligible, evidenced business losses under the actual policy wording; heat is covered only if its cause and loss meet that wording.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Eligible reimbursement may preserve cash flow and jobs; this is a possible mechanism.
instruments.risk_holder: Insurer/reinsurer for accepted claims; business for exclusions and deductibles.
instruments.speed: After evidence and adjustment; no heat-specific observed timing verified.
instruments.typical_cost: Premium, deductible, waiting period and compliance costs; no verified heat-specific tariff.
instruments.strengths: Can reflect actual insured financial loss.
instruments.limits: Ordinary business interruption may require insured physical damage; heat alone must not be assumed covered.
instruments.basis_risk: Coverage and loss-definition mismatch rather than weather-index basis risk.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Small informal firms may lack accounts, contracts or insurable cover; local evidence is needed.

instruments.name: Crop yield-loss indemnity / area-yield cover
instruments.plain_definition: Compensates eligible yield shortfall under notified crop and area rules. An area-yield contract uses average area yield, not each farm's loss.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Can reduce borrowing after eligible harvest losses.
instruments.risk_holder: Insurer/reinsurer and applicable public support; farmer retains excluded losses.
instruments.who_pays: Farmer plus public subsidy where applicable.
instruments.speed: Dependent on crop-cutting/yield data and settlement; seasonal timing may miss immediate heat needs.
instruments.typical_cost: Farmer premium, public subsidy and loss-assessment costs; no universal heat price.
instruments.limits: PMFBY is included as a direct yield-loss design model; specific heat eligibility is not verified by the source's named-peril list.
instruments.basis_risk: Area-yield averages can miss a particular farm's loss; heat cause may be disputed.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Documentation, crop/area notification and enrolment determine access; landless workers do not gain wage cover.

instruments.name: Livestock death or loss indemnity
instruments.plain_definition: Reimburses the eligible insured loss of livestock, after veterinary and policy checks.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: An accepted claim could prevent distress borrowing or sale of productive assets.
instruments.risk_holder: Insurer; farmer retains deductibles, exclusions and uninsured yield loss.
instruments.speed: Requires loss evidence; no heat-specific settlement benchmark verified.
instruments.typical_cost: Premium, excess, veterinary evidence and administration; not verified for heat.
instruments.strengths: Can match an eligible animal loss.
instruments.limits: Heat death, reduced milk yield and disease are distinct coverages; no primary heat indemnity wording verified here.
instruments.basis_risk: No index basis risk in individual loss adjustment; substantial coverage and valuation risk.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Eligibility and premium support need contract review.

instruments.name: Health expense indemnity and employment-injury protection
instruments.plain_definition: Health indemnity reimburses eligible expenses; employment-injury systems provide specified medical or earnings benefits where heat illness qualifies.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Eligible health and earnings benefits can reduce medical debt and income loss.
instruments.risk_holder: Health insurer or social insurance institution under scheme rules.
instruments.who_pays: Household, employer, social contributions or public funds.
instruments.who_receives: Patient, provider or eligible worker, depending on benefit.
instruments.speed: Cashless care and reimbursement have different timing; no generic heat benchmark.
instruments.typical_cost: Premium/contribution, co-payments, exclusions and administration vary.
instruments.strengths: Responds to diagnosed illness rather than an outdoor temperature alone.
instruments.limits: Not all health-related insurance is indemnity: the Japanese example is a fixed clinical-event benefit.
instruments.basis_risk: No weather-index mismatch; diagnosis, access and eligibility can still exclude heat harm.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Access depends on coverage and care availability; informal workers need explicit inclusion.

instruments.name: Fixed benefit for a heat-related clinical event
instruments.plain_definition: Pays a set amount for a covered medical event such as qualifying heatstroke treatment; it is neither weather-parametric nor expense indemnity.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Can offset treatment-related costs after an eligible event.
instruments.risk_holder: Insurer for the scheduled benefit; patient for remaining costs.
instruments.speed: After clinical documentation; observed settlement time not verified.
instruments.typical_cost: Policy-specific premium; no cost benchmark included.
instruments.limits: Cannot finance prevention before illness; clinical access shapes who can claim.
instruments.basis_risk: No weather basis risk; harm without the specified clinical event can go unpaid.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Digital enrolment and access to qualifying treatment may exclude people; no transferability of eligibility assumed.

instruments.name: Regional sovereign insurance pool
instruments.plain_definition: Countries use shared insurance infrastructure and risk capital, often with reinsurance, to finance agreed disaster losses.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Pooling and pre-agreed response plans can improve access to liquidity; heat requires explicit cover.
instruments.risk_holder: Pool insurer, reinsurers and governments for residual risk.
instruments.who_receives: Insured government; people receive funds only through a further delivery step.
instruments.speed: Lao PDR verified sovereign receipt benchmark is in its scheme record; it is not household timing.
instruments.typical_cost: Lao policy cost and limit are recorded separately; no heat premium verified.
instruments.strengths: Shares capacity, infrastructure and contingency planning.
instruments.limits: Diversification may weaken for correlated regional heat; no pool heat payout verified here.
instruments.basis_risk: Index/impact reporting may miss losses and uncounted people.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Needs an inclusive public spending plan and accessible channels.

instruments.name: Catastrophe bonds and insurance-linked securities
instruments.plain_definition: Investors place capital at risk; an agreed disaster trigger releases some or all protection to the sponsor.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: A tail-risk receipt can reduce emergency fiscal pressure.
instruments.risk_holder: Investors for contracted principal at risk; sponsor for residual loss.
instruments.who_pays: Sponsor pays risk-transfer costs; investors receive contractual returns.
instruments.speed: Calculation and settlement govern receipt; announcement is not proof of receipt.
instruments.typical_cost: Risk margin, structuring, modelling and issuance costs; Jamaica terms are a non-heat example.
instruments.strengths: Can provide multi-year external risk capital.
instruments.limits: No heat catastrophe bond verified; deal scale and trigger validation may be barriers.
instruments.basis_risk: Parametric or modelled-loss trigger may diverge from real loss.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: A bond has no automatic household entitlement.

instruments.name: Contingent disaster credit
instruments.plain_definition: A pre-agreed credit line can be drawn when legal and programme conditions are satisfied.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Pre-approved borrowing can reduce disruptive emergency reallocations.
instruments.risk_holder: Borrower retains loss and repayment obligations; lender supplies liquidity.
instruments.who_pays: Government repays principal, interest and applicable fees.
instruments.speed: Available after drawdown conditions and request; household transfer timing is separate.
instruments.typical_cost: Interest, commitment/front-end or other applicable fees and debt-service costs; dated contract terms required.
instruments.limits: Debt headroom and declarations can constrain use; heat eligibility is contract-specific.
instruments.basis_risk: No insurance basis risk, but a harmful event may not satisfy drawdown conditions.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Only through funded services or inclusive transfers.

instruments.name: Contingency budgets
instruments.plain_definition: Public spending authority is agreed before a shock so funds can be redirected or released under specified rules.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Delegated authority can fund staff, cooling, water and outreach before ad hoc approvals delay action.
instruments.who_receives: Authorised departments, suppliers and transfer recipients.
instruments.speed: Can be quick only if authority, cash and procurement are ready; no universal observed speed.
instruments.typical_cost: Opportunity cost and administration; a budget entry is not necessarily cash.
instruments.strengths: Can cover common heat needs without insurance attachment.
instruments.limits: Other emergencies compete for allocations; no dedicated city heat contingency appropriation verified here.
instruments.basis_risk: No insurance index basis risk; allocation and targeting errors remain.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Needs explicit entitlement or accessible service provision.

instruments.name: Reserves and dedicated disaster funds
instruments.plain_definition: Cash or legally earmarked resources are held for eligible disaster spending; dedicated heat funds require explicit rules.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: A replenished reserve can fund recurring response without repeated budget disruption.
instruments.speed: Depends on release rules, liquidity and procurement; no verified heat-specific service standard.
instruments.typical_cost: Opportunity cost of holding resources, replenishment and administration.
instruments.strengths: Suitable for retained losses and needs that contracts do not cover.
instruments.limits: Fund existence does not prove heat eligibility or actual cash availability.
instruments.basis_risk: No insurance basis risk; legal and administrative gaps can block relief.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Eligibility and accessible delivery determine reach.

instruments.name: Humanitarian anticipatory action / forecast-based finance
instruments.plain_definition: A forecast meeting agreed conditions releases pre-arranged resources for specified early actions.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Finances prevention or cash before the anticipated peak rather than waiting for damage.
instruments.risk_holder: Humanitarian fund bears intervention cost; communities retain residual harm.
instruments.who_pays: Donors and pooled-fund contributors; not necessarily an insurance premium.
instruments.who_receives: National society, NGOs, suppliers and selected households.
instruments.speed: Must fit forecast lead time; action lead time is not verified household cash timing.
instruments.typical_cost: Readiness, data, prepositioning, transfer delivery and false-alarm costs.
instruments.strengths: Can finance public-health action without an insured asset.
instruments.limits: Limited geographic coverage and donor replenishment; forecasts can be wrong.
instruments.basis_risk: Forecast false positives and missed events; targeting error is distinct.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Bangladesh protocol targets vulnerable urban residents; full eligibility coverage is not established.

instruments.name: National anticipatory finance
instruments.plain_definition: A government pre-agrees forecasts, actions and public release authority for acting before expected heat.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Connects national warnings with funded local action.
instruments.who_receives: Authorised agencies and people through agreed channels.
instruments.speed: Forecast-to-action window must exceed delivery time; not verified for a specific national heat treasury facility.
instruments.typical_cost: Readiness, forecasting, authorisation and delivery costs; no universal unit cost.
instruments.strengths: Could institutionalise action beyond project cycles.
instruments.limits: National-system design is not established merely because a humanitarian protocol operates nationally.
instruments.basis_risk: Forecast error plus administrative and targeting risk.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Requires registries, outreach and provision for unregistered people.

instruments.name: Shock-responsive social protection
instruments.plain_definition: An existing benefit system increases payments or temporarily adds eligible people after a pre-agreed shock.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: A ready payment channel can preserve consumption and reduce harmful coping.
instruments.risk_holder: Government and financing partners; households retain unmet needs.
instruments.who_pays: Public budgets, grants and any linked financing.
instruments.speed: Depends on updated registries, enrolment and payment access; drought-system timing is not a heat benchmark.
instruments.typical_cost: Transfer value plus registration, verification, delivery, appeals and financing.
instruments.strengths: Can extend beyond insured workers to non-working vulnerable people.
instruments.limits: Existing exclusions can expand during a shock; employment-linked transfers may require unsafe work.
instruments.basis_risk: Index false negatives plus registry and benefit-adequacy errors.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Horizontal expansion can include previously uncovered people only if funded and operational.

instruments.name: Contributory bad-weather wage replacement
instruments.plain_definition: A social insurance arrangement compensates eligible work stoppages due to dangerous weather, including heat where explicitly covered.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Preserves earnings when work must stop, reducing the financial barrier to rest.
instruments.risk_holder: Social insurance fund and covered employers under scheme rules.
instruments.who_pays: Employer and worker contributions in the Algerian example.
instruments.who_receives: Eligible workers, potentially through employer payroll.
instruments.speed: Payroll and reimbursement deadlines require current administrator verification.
instruments.typical_cost: Contributions and administrative costs; exact Algerian rate excluded pending accessible primary confirmation.
instruments.strengths: Recognises income loss before medical injury.
instruments.limits: Contributory employment rules may exclude informal and unregistered workers.
instruments.basis_risk: Eligibility and recognition of a work stoppage can miss actual harm.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Formal-sector protection is verified in ILO guidance; informal inclusion not verified.

instruments.name: Premium support and smart subsidies
instruments.plain_definition: Public or donor money pays part of an insurance premium; design can target affordability while funding transparency and review.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Can improve access to risk transfer without requiring the poorest to pay the full premium.
instruments.risk_holder: Underlying insurer retains contracted risk; sponsor bears subsidy cost.
instruments.who_pays: Government or donor; policy buyer may pay the balance.
instruments.who_receives: Insurer receives premium; insured receives only eligible benefits.
instruments.speed: Premium is paid at inception/renewal; this is not a disaster payout.
instruments.typical_cost: Subsidy plus targeting, administration and evaluation; grants may also fund technical assistance.
instruments.strengths: Can address affordability and build accessible distribution.
instruments.limits: Renewal dependency, weak customer value and poorly targeted subsidies are possible; not findings about a named provider.
instruments.basis_risk: Does not remove basis risk; may subsidise a mismatched trigger.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Must identify who benefits and provide fallback for non-enrollees.

examples.text: Lao PDR premium support is reported by World Bank; wider grant support must not all be labelled premium.

instruments.name: Results-based / outcome-linked heat payments
instruments.plain_definition: A funder pays for verified outputs or outcomes under an agreed contract; financing must bridge the time before verification.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Could reward maintained protection or verified cooling delivery; avoided harm attribution requires care.
instruments.risk_holder: Implementer bears performance/cash-flow risk unless advances are agreed.
instruments.who_pays: Outcome funder; an investor may bridge costs but is not necessarily the ultimate payer.
instruments.speed: Generally after verification; not suitable alone for urgent household liquidity.
instruments.typical_cost: Working capital, monitoring, independent verification and administration.
instruments.strengths: Can link payment to service performance.
instruments.limits: No verified heat-health outcome-payment deal found; energy savings are not proof of lives saved.
instruments.basis_risk: Performance-metric mismatch and attribution risk, not weather basis risk.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Depends on service eligibility; incentives may otherwise favour easier-to-reach populations.

narrative.title: The instrument map
narrative.text: Heat finance is a portfolio of funding sources, contracts, authorisations and delivery channels. The 19 categories below distinguish actual heat applications from non-heat models and unverified heat concepts. Risk transfer covers a contracted liability; reserves and borrowing leave the underlying loss with the holder. Anticipatory action describes timing and pre-agreed action. Social protection describes a benefit system and delivery route. Premium support changes who pays for insurance. Results-based finance rewards verified performance and is usually not emergency liquidity. These dimensions overlap, so their money must not be added as if each were an additional protection benefit.
narrative.known: Verified heat applications exist at household, employer and humanitarian-programme levels.
narrative.inferred: A useful Common Shade map should let users distinguish funding source, recipient, release condition and delivery channel.
narrative.uncertain: No issued sovereign heat policy, heat catastrophe bond or heat-health outcome-payment contract was verified in this review. This is a search finding, not evidence that none exists.

narrative.title: Risk layering for heat
narrative.text: Start with a costed response plan, not an insurance product. Retain the cost of frequent needs through budgets and replenishable reserves. Use contingent credit for liquidity needs that justify borrowing and meet drawdown conditions. Consider insurance/reinsurance or capital-market transfer for financially severe, less frequent residual losses. These are tendencies, not fixed return-period boundaries. Timing overlays every layer: forecast releases can fund early action, while ready benefit systems, payroll and public services can deliver support. World Bank guidance describes this layered approach. The Philippines Cat DDO example demonstrates declaration-linked liquidity; SEADRIF demonstrates an impact-linked sovereign receipt. Neither reviewed example proves heat eligibility. For cities, borrowing authority, transfers from national government and procurement rules must be checked separately. Heat's recurring income and clinical costs need routine funding even when no rare-event policy triggers. Prevention remains a recurrent public and employer responsibility. A warming climate also means pricing and attachment assumptions need review, rather than automatic extrapolation from historical loss frequencies.
narrative.designer_description: Draw a tall rectangle with loss severity increasing upward and frequency decreasing upward. Put budgets/reserves at the broad base, contingent credit in the middle, and insurance/reinsurance/capital-market cover at the top. Do not assign numerical return periods without a local fiscal loss model. Place a continuous prevention-and-readiness strip underneath. Beside the stack, show a time axis: forecast, action, event, index confirmation, treasury/agency receipt, household/service receipt. Overlay anticipatory finance across the pre-event part and social-protection/payroll/service channels across the full stack. Label the gap between a warning and action authority, and the gap between institution receipt and final delivery. Add an explicit fallback path for harm below insurance thresholds. Do not draw premiums as additional payout capital or add borrowing to grants without showing repayment.
narrative.known: Different instruments can finance different severities and phases; source availability alone does not ensure delivery.
narrative.inferred: For heat, the recurring budget and last-mile capability may be more foundational than an upper risk-transfer layer.
narrative.uncertain: Optimal attachment points, reserve size, premium affordability and borrowing capacity require local data and an agreed response liability.

narrative.title: Why heat needs different financing designs
narrative.text: Heat can create serious health and livelihood losses without destroying an asset. Harm can develop quickly within a prolonged hot period, and cumulative days and nights matter. Ambient temperature alone does not represent humidity, radiant load, work intensity or indoor exposure. Mortality under-reporting complicates both loss assessment and trigger calibration. These facts support a separation between public-health warnings, permission and resources to act, and contractual payout triggers. They do not establish that any one index is universally superior.
narrative.known: Heat-health risk depends on exposure, duration and vulnerability; under-reporting and delayed delivery can obscure need.
narrative.inferred: Different response costs may warrant different trigger families and a lower-threshold retained fallback.
narrative.uncertain: The best local index, station/grid resolution, verification method and health-income calibration cannot be specified from a global map.

narrative.title: What can be said about the heat protection gap
narrative.text: No verified Asia-wide estimate matching heat-specific economic losses to heat-specific insured compensation was found. The nearest auditable regional comparison here is Swiss Re sigma 1/2025, table 3: Asia's 2024 disaster-event economic losses were USD 66.5 billion and insured losses USD 11.1 billion. Subtracting the rounded figures gives approximately USD 55.4 billion uninsured, or 83.3%. This table includes natural and man-made disasters and is not a heat estimate. Its economic-loss definition emphasises direct damage and property-related business interruption; it excludes wider indirect earnings/GDP and non-economic losses, and its insured-loss definition excludes life and liability. The dataset covers 104 qualifying Asian disaster events, not a population sample. Source currency is USD, price year 2024, conversion in this report 1 USD = 1 USD. Underlying foreign-currency losses were converted by sigma using occurrence-year end exchange rates and inflation-adjusted as described in its methods. Event-level original currencies and rates were not reproduced in the regional aggregate. Kind: economic-loss estimate, insured-loss estimate and calculated uninsured-loss estimate-not premiums, limits or bank-confirmed payouts. No counterfactual baseline is applicable. These scope limits make the statistic an especially poor proxy for heat mortality, daily wages or informal work.
narrative.known: A broad regional uninsured-loss comparison is available; its scope is explicitly wider in hazards and narrower in welfare losses than the question about heat.
narrative.inferred: A heat-finance gap assessment should separately measure unfunded response costs, uncovered income/health harm and delays in delivery.
narrative.uncertain: Asia's heat-specific insured share and the amount reaching affected people before harmful coping remain unquantified here.

narrative.title: Evidence and publication boundary
narrative.text: This is a targeted, source-linked landscape map checked on 31 October 2026, not an exhaustive systematic review or a contract-level due-diligence certification. Searches prioritised South and Southeast Asia, then Africa, Middle East and Latin America, with Hong Kong and Japan retained for specific transferable design lessons. English searches were supplemented by Japanese primary product documentation and French administrator leads. Missing primary access is recorded, not silently replaced by a claim of verification. Historical policy-year records are separated from current programme availability. Loop/lever mappings and possible causal pathways are analytical interpretations; they are not evidence that any scheme has changed a feedback loop. No comparative ranking was undertaken.
narrative.known: Reported payment activity is not equivalent to an evaluated health or income effect. The J-PAL page describes a randomized encouragement evaluation design; reviewed material does not report its results.
narrative.inferred: Publication should distinguish existence, contractual design, actual cash receipt and measured effect as separate filters.
narrative.uncertain: Current renewals, full trigger schedules, customer complaints, rejection rates and subgroup access remain incompletely documented.

heat_design_challenges.challenge: Health and income harm without damaged assets
heat_design_challenges.design_used: SEWA income-oriented parametric cover; separate public/social benefits and heatstroke clinical benefits address other losses.
heat_design_challenges.remaining_gap: These mechanisms cover different needs. A clinical-event payment is not wages and a fixed benefit is not full expense indemnity.

heat_design_challenges.design_used: Reviewed operational heat examples use weather or forecasts rather than requiring a counted heat death.
heat_design_challenges.remaining_gap: This bypasses death-certification delay but does not make payouts track mortality. Mortality surveillance and excess-mortality analysis remain relevant for calibration; no operational excess-mortality heat payout trigger verified.

heat_design_challenges.challenge: Accumulation across consecutive days and nights
heat_design_challenges.design_used: Multi-day triggers are used in SEWA and AXA designs; historical Pakistan DRF learning considered maximum and minimum temperatures.
heat_design_challenges.remaining_gap: Long consecutive-day requirements may miss intermittent severe exposure; hot-night-specific payment wording not verified for current examples.

heat_design_challenges.design_used: Start Network's Pakistan design describes a GFS-based heat-index model; Bangladesh activation references heat index alongside temperature.
heat_design_challenges.remaining_gap: Heat index is not WBGT. Neither automatically captures workload, radiant heat, clothing or indoor conditions. Exact current algorithms require review.

heat_design_challenges.challenge: Sparse stations and coarse exposure data
heat_design_challenges.design_used: SEWA's first pilot used NASA POWER; provider examples also use official weather observations.
heat_design_challenges.remaining_gap: Gridded/reanalysis data are not local ground measurement or satellite land-surface temperature. Independent local validation, missing-data rules and a backup feed are proposed safeguards, not verified scheme features.

heat_design_challenges.challenge: Warning, action and payout are separate
heat_design_challenges.design_used: Humanitarian EAPs pre-agree actions and finance; lower-threshold assistance can sit beside insurance.
heat_design_challenges.remaining_gap: Record forecast issue, trigger confirmation, release approval, institutional receipt and final receipt separately; an action lead time is not cash-in-hand speed.

heat_design_challenges.challenge: Forecast false alarms and missed harm
heat_design_challenges.design_used: Start Network reports a historical Karachi activation where the predicted threshold event did not materialise; preventative activities continued.
heat_design_challenges.remaining_gap: False positives have costs; misses can leave harm unfunded. No universal acceptable error rate or independently measured basis-risk rate is established.
